GrooveLinx
Five roles, one band · real screens
One band · five jobs · every screen real

A band is really five jobs. This is the one system that runs them all.

The player learning the songs, the leader booking the shows, the keeper of the recordings, the producer running load-in, the woodshedder grinding alone at home. Pick a role and follow its week — every screen below is the live app on real DeadCetera data, no mockups.

Captured from the running app across phone, desktop & iPad.

🎸 The Player’s Week · glance → learn → rehearse → perform

The week

📱 PhoneStep 01 · In your pocket

“What’s coming up — and are we behind?”

A spare minute before work. Old way: dig through a group chat to reconstruct the schedule.

One screen answers it: the next gig, how ready the band is for it, and the exact song dragging you down.

✦
Home dashboard
The next gig, a live Band Readiness meter, upcoming events, and today’s practice suggestions — the whole week at a glance.
▸ Drill one level deeper 3 features
Weakest-link callout
“48% · 11 things left · weakest: Iko Iko” — it names the one song holding the set back, not a vague to-do.
Notifications + Band Feed
New charts, plan changes, and messages land here so nobody’s out of the loop.
Mode switch
Flip the whole app into rehearsal or performance mindset from the top bar.
dev.groovelinx.com
🖥 DesktopStep 02 · At home, the big screen

“How does this one actually go?”

Old way: rewind a YouTube video a dozen times, losing your place in the chart every time.

Open the chart and pull the lesson up right on top of it — a hand-picked how-to or the band’s reference version, floating over the chords while you read them. Loop and half-speed are built in; you never leave the song.

✦
Chart + lesson, one screen
Float a “how to play” video (or the North Star version) over the live chart. A/B-loop the tricky bar, drop to half speed, and read the chords the teacher is playing — at the same time.
▸ Drill one level deeper 3 features
Docked over the chart
Move it, resize it, or pin it to a bar — the chart stays readable behind it.
Loop the hard four bars at half speed
Set A/B markers, drop to 0.5x, and grind the one phrase until it sticks.
Every video for the song
The North Star, backing tracks, and jam-section breakdowns are all one tap from the chart.
dev.groovelinx.com
🖥 DesktopStep 03 · The chart, your way

“Give me the chart — in my key, for my instrument.”

Old way: a photo of a crumpled chart in the wrong key, squinting to find your part.

A clean full-screen chart. Transpose in one tap. Flip between the shared band chart and your own personal layer without losing the song.

✦
Chart reader — transpose + Group / Just Me
Big, readable chart with instant transpose (♭ 0 ♯) and a live toggle between the band’s shared chart (“Group”) and your personal version (“Just Me”).
▸ Drill one level deeper 3 features
The Mix
A chart is layers you mute and solo like stems — Lyrics, Chords, Tab, Harmony, Cues, Notes. Keep the band’s lyrics, drop the chords, add your own tab on top.
Import a tab from Ultimate Guitar
Search UG ranked to your instrument, pick the version you trust, one tap pulls it into your layer — no copy-paste.
Sized for a music stand
Font up/down and zoom so it’s legible from playing distance, not phone distance.
📲 iPadStep 04 · What to actually work on

“Don’t re-run the whole song — fix the rough part.”

Old way: play it top to bottom three times and hope the weak spot fixes itself.

Each song carries its own plan, tuned to the band. It knows who’s behind and tells you exactly where the minutes should go.

✦
Today’s Rehearsal Plan (per song, per member)
A time-boxed plan for this song — “Band’s at 2.0, not stage-ready,” “Pierce hasn’t learned this yet (1/5), give them space,” “full run-through.”
▸ Drill one level deeper 3 features
Practice tasks
A rough moment flagged in review becomes a checkable task pinned to the song — the loop from “that fell apart” to “fixed.”
Run Through vs Practice
One button to play it straight through, one to drill the hard section — the app knows which you need.
Parts & Stems
Isolate the harmony or a single instrument to learn your part against the others.
📲 iPadStep 05 · In the room

“Keep us moving — and on the right things.”

Rehearsals stall on “what’s next?” and drift onto songs that are already fine.

Build next week’s rehearsal from what the gig actually needs and what’s actually weak — then run it, on the clock.

✦
Build the rehearsal
Assemble a set from smart buckets — a Jam to open, the Gig songs, the ones that need tightening, something new — with a running time estimate.
▸ Drill one level deeper 3 features
Start here: top 5 to focus on
The five songs that need work before the show, each with its readiness %, ready to drop into the plan.
“I can start one for you”
Hand the planning to the app and just play.
Plan change history
Every past plan state is kept as a read-only audit — nothing’s ever lost when you rebuild.
📲 iPadStep 06 · The killer workflow

“Listen back — where were we tight, where did it fall apart?”

The best of rehearsal evaporates on the drive home. By Tuesday nobody remembers the rough spot.

The whole rehearsal is captured and laid out song by song. Scrub to the one that got away and hear exactly what happened. This is the workflow the whole app is built to feed.

✦
Rehearsal Review
Play back each song from your own recording, see where the band was tight and where it got rough, tap a song for detail, double-tap to loop a bar.
▸ Drill one level deeper 3 features
It matches the recording for you
Tell it “Band Rehearsal,” “Live Gig,” or “Individual Practice” and it lines the audio up against your plan or setlist automatically.
A comment becomes a task
Flag “bridge fell apart at 4:02” and it turns into a Practice Task on that song — review feeds the next rehearsal.
It becomes band memory
Every session is kept, so “are we actually getting better?” has a real answer.
📲 iPadStep 07 · On the stand, under the lights

“Everything I need on stage — nothing I don’t.”

Under stage lights you can’t fumble tabs, tiny text, or the wrong key.

Live Gig Mode: the current song big and readable, hands-free auto-scroll, your key locked in, and the next song always in view.

✦
Live Gig Mode
Full-screen performance chart with auto-scroll (and speed control), one-tap transpose, the BPM, and “coming up → …” so you’re never caught off guard.
▸ Drill one level deeper 3 features
Works with no signal
Before you start, “top up cache” downloads every chart so the venue’s dead Wi-Fi can’t touch you.
One key, locked in
Transpose is remembered per band-and-song; scroll speed and font are per device — set once, trusted all night.
Jump anywhere
Set the running order, or jump to any song when the crowd calls an audible.

🖥 DesktopStep 05 · The money

“The gig paid — now the awkward part.”

Gig payouts + settle-up

The week

📲 iPadStep 01 · After the session

“We recorded it — now make it useful.”

Old way: a voice-memo blob nobody ever opens again.

Point GrooveLinx at the recording and tell it what it was — it lines the audio up against the plan or setlist and turns a raw take into reviewable songs.

✦
Recording ingest
Band rehearsal, live gig, or solo practice — it matches the audio to your plan or setlist and splits it into per-song segments you can actually review.
▸ Drill one level deeper 3 features
Straight off the board
Ingest a full X32 multitrack — 18 tracks — not just a phone recording.
Auto-segmented into songs
It finds the song boundaries so you’re not scrubbing a 70-minute file.
Feeds the whole loop
Every ingest becomes reviewable, and a flagged moment becomes a Practice Task.
dev.groovelinx.com
🖥 DesktopStep 02 · Parts in isolation

“I need to hear just the bass on that turnaround.”

Old way: you can’t un-hear the full mix to catch one part.

Separate any recording into isolated tracks — drums, bass, vocals, keys, guitar — to study exactly what someone played.

✦
Stem separation (Demucs)
A 4- or 6-stem split on a GPU in about 30 seconds — paste a URL or upload a file. Solo the part you’re learning, mute the one you’re replacing.
▸ Drill one level deeper 3 features
6-stem model
Adds keys and guitar on top of drums / bass / vocals / other.
Pan-check first
Peek at the stereo field before spending a separation.
Self-hosted, cents per song
~$0.005 a track — no per-seat subscription.
dev.groovelinx.com

Set one North Star per song — the definitive reference the whole band aims at — and the app builds a canon out of them.

North Stars
The band’s reference canon, 44 songs deep, Spotify or YouTube, with “Play All” and Listen-Together so everyone syncs to the exact same target.

The week

📱 PhoneStep 01 · Before a note

“Start in tune, or waste the hour.”

Old way: a separate tuner app you have to go dig for.

A real chromatic tuner built right in — pick your instrument and tuning, and a reference tone for every string is a tap away.

✦
Tuner
Meter, dial, or strobe display; instrument and tuning presets; tap any string to hear its reference pitch — in the same app as everything else.
▸ Drill one level deeper 3 features
Three displays
Meter, dial, or strobe — whichever you read fastest.
Alternate tunings

Reference tones
Tap a string to hear where it should sit.
📱 PhoneStep 02 · The hard truth

“If it falls apart, it’s usually time.”

Old way: practicing the rush until it becomes a habit.

A metronome set to the song’s BPM, with subdivisions and a trainer that nudges you faster a few clicks at a time.

✦
Metronome + trainer
BPM dial, time signatures, subdivisions, and tap tempo — plus a trainer that steps the tempo up every few bars until the part is automatic.
